memories.content: Calculate user study compensation budgets based on estimated participation burden, combining session time and preparation effort.
Compensate for required travel time in face-to-face user studies as well.
Compensate for the actual time participants spent in sessions, regardless of research modality.
Leave cash payment as an available compensation method for face-to-face studies.
If compensation equity is explained, do not require finalizing the payment method at the proposal stage.
Apply the same base hourly rate to face-to-face and remote studies if task burden is equal.
Participants judge compensation fairness based on the total burden, combining session time with required travel and preparation time.
Account in compensation for the burden of rescheduling iterations and returning for multiple formative evaluation sessions.
Compensate participants for time already invested even if a session is terminated early due to prototype errors.
The author of this proposal tends to exclude preparation burden between sessions when calculating compensation for iterative studies.
List whom to notify and in what order if serious discomfort is reported during the study.
Field staff rely on the pre-defined contact sequence when serious discomfort is reported.
Define the thresholds for participant harm, operational disruption, and data anomalies at which deployment and data collection must cease.
Establish procedures to restore existing systems and workflow states after suspending field deployment.
The user's stop plan can be judged feasible only when it identifies who has authority to order recovery and who is responsible for carrying it out.

In organizations where error reporting is linked to individual performance evaluations, safety signal records may be separated from research decision logs, potentially breaking the traceability path for the same incident.

analysis.overview: The frames address separate operational domains. The reference frame covers equitable participant compensation and burden accounting, while the compared frame covers safety escalation, stopping criteria, recovery governance, and incident traceability; neither contains a scope-aligned counterpart to the other’s claims.

reports.compared_only: The compared frame addresses discomfort escalation, mandatory stop thresholds, system restoration, recovery authority and responsibility, and organizational risks to incident traceability.
reports.reference_only: The reference frame addresses compensation budgeting, burden components, modality equity, payment flexibility, iterative participation, early termination, and a preparation-time omission risk.
